name: astral-3d
description: The Thermo Astral analyser: an asymmetric-track multi-reflection time-of-flight instrument, modelled entirely from published information. Two elongated mirrors face each other across a 41.43 mm board gap; ions oscillate between them while drifting along their length, and the mirrors converge slightly so the drift decelerates and reverses. Each mirror is a two-dimensional cross-section whose extrusion axis is tilted by half the convergence, which makes the field anisotropy Ez/Ex exactly tan(alpha) instead of a quantity no affordable three-dimensional mesh can resolve - see docs/astral-log.md sections 12 and 13. The two solves carry one mirror at potential with the other grounded, which is the ordinary basis decomposition and therefore exact. The ion foil is not included: its shape is measured in section 11 and the drift force it produced was 5.7 times what the published reversal needs, so it is a study rather than part of the shipped device. The third element is the ion foil: a volume solve carrying the four plates carrying sixteen slice biases fitted to the published drift pseudopotential with every mirror strip grounded, which is the basis field psi_foil. The tilt supplies a0 = 0.84 of the drift pseudopotential and the stripe the remaining 0.16, which Grinfeld et al. give in closed form; an earlier revision of this template said the tilt was only 31 to 38 per cent of what was needed, and that was an artefact of a tilt baseline wrong by a factor of two. Measured here at a0 = 0.8504 against the published 0.83999. The mirror electrodes are placed from the design paper's Fig. 1 (five per mirror, with gaps, electrode 0 grounded) and carry the crowd-control paper's Table 1 voltages with the sign of U2 corrected to positive; the board gap, U3 and U4 are solved for the design paper's own three-point condition - the drift period stationary at 4000 eV and at 4000 plus or minus 100 - giving a 41.43 mm gap, U3 0.9740 against the table's 0.916 and U4 1.4815 against 1.503. There the mirror reproduces the published period-slope curve, and the published on-axis potential to 0.159 kV rms at sixteen points, which is a check the solve never saw. See docs/astral-log.md sections 58-65.

ionEnergy.description: Nominal beam energy. Stewart et al.: 4 keV entering the analyser.

spacerThickness.description: Thickness of the spacer that tilts the mirrors relative to one another. PUBLISHED: Stewart et al. give 200 microns. What it is not published over is the baseline - see tiltBaseline - and that is the whole of the uncertainty in the drift reversal.

tiltBaseline.description: Length the spacer tilts each mirror over, so the tilt angle is asin(spacerThickness / tiltBaseline). PUBLISHED as of 2026-09-04: Grinfeld et al. give the convergence as 0.045 deg BETWEEN the mirrors, which over a 0.2 mm spacer is a 509.3 mm baseline. Two independent routes agree - requiring the tilt to supply the published a0 = 0.83999 of the drift pseudopotential wants 515.9 mm, 1.3% away. This was 250 mm and flagged as the most consequential guess in the reconstruction, carrying a 2.8-fold ambiguity; it was wrong by almost exactly a factor of two.

injectionAngle.description: Tangent of the angle between the trajectory and the mirror axis, setting the drift rate as V tan(theta). PUBLISHED as of 2026-09-04: Grinfeld et al. Table 1 gives a nominal 1.78 deg, and this is its tangent. Was 0.03998 (2.29 deg), inferred by requiring the reversal to land at 335 mm with the tilt baseline also wrong - the two errors compensated, which is why the geometric register reproduced anyway.

driftLength.description: Extent along the drift, and hence the extent of the foil. Published nominal drift is 335 mm, but this must be LONGER: where the stripe ends its contribution to the drift potential decays and partly cancels the tilt's continuing rise, leaving a crest an ion with slightly more sideways energy can clear. With the foil coextensive with a 350 mm drift that crest sat 2.3% above the nominal drift energy while the design's operating range is 2.2%, and the reversal jumped from 338.6 to 409.1 mm for a 1.1% change in injection angle. At 450 mm the crest moves to 435 mm and demands 6.3 V against the ion's 4.8. See docs/astral-log.md section 48.

capToCap.description: Cap plate to cap plate. 720 puts the cap 360 mm from the mid-plane, 5 mm past electrode 4. The effective mirror separation the paper quotes (641 mm) is set by the electrode positions and voltages, not by the cap, and measures 656 at this geometry - 2.3 per cent long, section 65.

boardGap.description: Distance between the two mirror boards across the beam. Published in neither paper. One of the three unknowns solved for the published three-point focusing condition (c1 = 0, c3 = 0, c2 = -1.25e-3 c4; handoff sections 70-71) together with U3 and U4, on a layout whose back wall and electrode-0 gap are read off the figure. It is also the gap at which a voltage fit to the published on-axis potential reproduced U1 to 1 per cent (section 62). Two routes, one number.

boardThickness.description: How thick each board is in y.

vacuumPad.description: Vacuum between the outermost metal and the solve boundary.

detectorInset.description: How far inside the far end the collecting plane sits.

mouth.description: Distance from the cap plate to the inner edge of electrode 1 - the mirror mouth. Derived from e1In so the foil expressions that reach the mirror keep meaning what they meant.

detectorZ.description: kept for reference: where a detector at the FAR end of the drift would sit. The shipped detector is behind the launch point instead, because an asymmetric-track analyser's ions drift out, reverse, and come back - catching them at the far end measures only the outbound half and hides the behaviour the device is named for.

mirrorTilt.description: Tilt of each mirror, in half turns. The near stack takes +mirrorTilt and the far -mirrorTilt, which brings both mouths toward the mid-plane as z increases.

zPad.description: how far the solve domain and the electrode stripes run beyond the drift at each end. The reversal convergence moves 7.4% from 0 to 50 mm and 0.4% from 50 to 150, so this is converged; at zero the Neumann face sits 10 mm from where the ion turns round.

foilVolts.description: Superseded by v0..v15; retained so older documents parse. Not referenced by any electrode.

foilThickness.description: how thick the foil electrodes are.

foilGap.description: Half-gap between the foil plates in the board-gap direction. Defaults to halfGap, so the foil is a shaped conductive region on the inner face of each board rather than a separate aperture in the flight path - which is both the plausible construction for a printed-circuit analyser and what the published schematic projects to. Mounting the plates flush costs 15% of the well depth (7.31 V against 8.58 V at foilGap 8 mm) and leaves the well shape unchanged, shallowest at 41% of the drift and deepest at 67%.

foilSlices.description: Number of constant-width boxes the contoured foil plate is built from. The contour runs along the drift, so each slice spans a range of drift and holds one inner-edge position.

foilOuterFrac.description: Foil plate outer edge, as a fraction of the mid-plane to mirror-mouth distance. Measured from the published schematic at 146 mm of 182 mm; the outer edge is straight to within one pixel over the whole drift.

foilInnerMid.description: Mean position of the foil plate inner edge, as a fraction of the mid-plane to mirror-mouth distance. The inner edge is contoured along the drift; this is the midpoint of that contour.

foilInnerAmplitude.description: Contour amplitude of the plate edge. Zero: the stripe shape is carried by the sixteen slice biases v0..v15 rather than by the plate outline, and both at once would say the same thing twice.

foilThinAt.description: Drift fraction at which the foil plate is thinnest, so its inner edge lies furthest from the axis and the gap between the two plates is widest.

foilThickAt.description: Drift fraction at which the foil plate is thickest, so its inner edge lies closest to the axis and the gap between the two plates is narrowest. Half a contour wavelength past foilThinAt.

foilStartFrac.description: Drift fraction at which the foil begins. The published figure shows the plates starting about a quarter of the way along, and that is what section 11 measured - but a foil that starts late cannot reverse the drift at all, because the net work a conservative axial field does is q(phi_start - phi_end) and an ion that crosses the whole potential bump nets nothing. Set to zero so the foil spans the drift and the ion begins inside it. Handoff section 15.

foilReach.description: Distance from the analyser mid-plane to a mirror mouth, the scale the foil plate positions are expressed as fractions of.

foilOuter.description: Foil plate outer edge, measured from the mid-plane.

foilDriftSpan.description: Fraction of the drift the foil covers.

foilGrade.description: Superseded by v0..v15; retained so older documents parse. Not referenced by any electrode.

convergence.description: How much the cap-to-cap gap narrows across the drift length. DERIVED from the spacer and its baseline, and reported because it is the quantity the earlier revisions of this template declared directly. 0.56 mm at the shipped values.

e0In.description: Inner edge of the grounded electrode 0, from the mid-plane. The schematic shows it running from the beam region out to electrode 1; 1 mm leaves the source at the mid-plane clear of it. Section 64 measured its extent as irrelevant to the focus.

e0Out.description: Outer edge of the grounded electrode 0, from the mid-plane. The figure shows a gap between electrodes 0 and 1; its lower panel draws only the live electrodes, so the width is not published. 8.6 mm - the width of the other small gaps - is what the on-axis potential across 150-230 mm chooses (section 71: rms 0.421 kV abutting, 0.228 at 8.6 mm, 0.263 at 12.3).

e1In.description: Inner edge of electrode 1, the accelerating lens. Measured pixel by pixel off Fig. 1 of Grinfeld et al. 2024 (NIM-A 1060, 169017), the grey blocks under the on-axis potential plot, at 500 dpi with both mirrors agreeing to 0.5 mm. Distance from the mid-plane between the mirrors. See docs/astral-log.md section 58.

e4Out.description: Outer edge of electrode 4, where it wraps round into the back wall of the mirror. The figure shows electrode 4 running past 347 mm off the plot edge and its upper panel shows the plate turning down into a wall, so the end of the mirror is at U4 rather than at earth. Where the earth was 11 mm behind a flat plate ending at 355, the axis at 340 mm read 4.75 kV against the figure 5.90 and the third-order coefficient was off by 0.17 (sections 70-71).

wallThickness.description: Thickness of the back wall electrode 4 wraps into. A guess; the wall screens the domain edge behind it, and the axis potential does not distinguish 360 from 395 mm.

v0.description: Stripe slice 0 of 16, its bias. The sixteen together approximate the published drift pseudopotential psi_s (Grinfeld et al. 2024, Fig. 4 and Eq. 15) as the stripe must supply it on top of what the mirror tilt gives: fitted by least squares over 0 to 400 mm on the shipped geometry, 0.24 per cent rms. A shape function would do better; sixteen segments hold the arrival time to R ~ 73,000 over the full acceptance (handoff section 56), which is adequate for the register and not for the instrument.
